nodes.content: Build a loop vectorizer preserving scalar semantics across data-dependent exits, potentially aliasing accesses, and faulting loads.
requirements: Preserve observable write ordering and precise faults without accessing memory beyond the scalar exit.
Achieve 1.3× throughput versus optimized scalar code on three representative loops combining exits and aliasing.

nodes.content: Guard chunk dereferenceability and disjointness, scan exits sequentially, mask live-lane loads, commit ordered stores; otherwise fall back to scalar.
When a store aliases a later exit-predicate load, can exit scanning precede ordered stores without changing the exit lane?
Earlier stores aliasing later predicate loads invalidate precommit scans; a cross-lane overlap guard with scalar fallback preserves exit lanes.
Implement cross-lane predicate/store overlap checks, sequential exit scans, and scalar fallback; validate fault addresses and store traces against scalar.
Run ExitAlias-12 differential tests with cross-lane predicate/store overlaps and guard pages; compare fallback decisions, exits, store traces, and faults.
ExitAlias-12 found 2/12 wrong exit lanes: range-based overlap guards missed indexed stores aliasing later predicate loads.
Precommit exit scans require dereference-free exact-address proofs, including indexed stores, excluding earlier-store/later-predicate overlaps; otherwise fall back to scalar.
Prove dereference-free cross-lane addresses and predicate-load safety; scan predicates sequentially, scalarize unprovable cases, rerun ExitAlias-12.
Compare range-guard and exact-address prototypes on ExitAlias-12, recording exit lanes, fallback choices, store traces, and guard-page faults.
Bounded-index overlap guards matched scalar exits, stores, and faults in 12/12 cases, vectorizing 4/12; exact-address proofs scalarized all.
Can bounded-index guards reach 1.3× optimized-scalar throughput on three exit-and-alias loops despite 8/12 ExitAlias-12 fallbacks?
Use indexed-store failures and validated bounded-index guards to benchmark three exit-alias kernels for ≥1.3× optimized-scalar speedup.
Using n13’s three indexed-store-derived kernels and scalar baseline, benchmark bounded-index versus exact-address guards; log speedups, exits, stores, faults.
Exact-address guards scalarized all three indexed-store kernels, matching scalar exits, store traces, and faults; speedups were 0.98–1.01×.
Select bounded-index guards with scalar fallback: naive ranges mis-exit; exact-address guards scalarize all three benchmark kernels.
Scalar-scan guarded predicates; vectorize dereferenceable exit-free prefixes, commit stores in order, and scalarize uncertain tails.
What proof permits batching prefix loads without bypassing earlier aliasing stores or reporting a later-lane fault first?
Batch only when dereference-free checks prove prefix loads cannot fault or overlap preceding writes; otherwise execute lanes in scalar order.
Benchmark guarded-prefix batching with scalar tails on ExitAlias-12 and three kernels; compare exits, store traces, first faults, and throughput.
ExitAlias-12 matched scalar exit lanes, store traces, first faults, and zero beyond-exit accesses; guarded-prefix speedups: 1.34×/1.38×/1.32×.
How can guards prove prefix loads nonfaulting for unknown pointer provenance without speculative dereferences or page-mapping assumptions?
Batch only within proven dereferenceable object bounds using checked offsets; scalarize unknown-provenance pointers and verify fault ordering with guard pages.
Implement checked-offset provenance guards; run guard-page ProvenanceFault-24 across bounded and unknown pointers, comparing scalar fault order and access traces.
ProvenanceFault-24 found 3/24 mismatched first faults: predicate scans faulted before earlier stores despite nonfaulting batched data loads.
Retain the 1.32–1.38× guarded-prefix path only when predicate scans are nonfaulting and independent of preceding stores; otherwise scalarize.
Batch only exit-free prefixes after proving predicate scans and loads nonfaulting and independent of earlier stores; otherwise scalarize.
Do stricter predicate-safety guards retain ≥1.3× throughput on all three kernels, or trigger excessive scalar fallback?
Implement stricter predicate guards; rerun ProvenanceFault-24 and benchmark three kernels versus prior 1.32–1.38×, recording fallbacks and faults.
Run ProvenanceFault-24 and three-kernel benchmarks with original and predicate-safe guards; record fault order, beyond-exit accesses, fallbacks, and scalar-relative speedups.
Predicate-safe guards achieved 1.27×/1.33×/1.31×; disjoint nonfaulting loads matched scalar, but 1/24 predicate scans crossed a faulting store.
Scalarize chunks with unproven store safety; test 4-lane guarded prefixes against the 1.27× kernel, then rerun fault and throughput benchmarks.
Implement 4-lane prefixes with scalar fallback for unproven predicate/store safety; rerun ProvenanceFault-24 and three-kernel fault/throughput benchmarks.
ProvenanceFault-24 matched scalar faults and stores 24/24 with zero beyond-exit accesses; 4-lane kernel speedups: 1.31×/1.34×/1.32×.
Adopt 4-lane predicate/store-safe prefixes with scalar fallback: all three kernels exceed 1.3×, and ProvenanceFault-24 matches scalar.
Use vector conflict detection and dereferenceability guards to dispatch safe first-exit-masked chunks; execute conflicting or fault-uncertain chunks scalar.
Can vector conflict detection identify indexed store-to-predicate hazards without evaluating faulting addresses or loads beyond the first scalar exit?
With arithmetic-only indices and proven-nonfaulting stores and predicates, checked-address conflict masks reject hazards before sequential exit scans and masked loads.
Implement checked-address conflict masks for arithmetic-only indices; scalarize unsafe stores or predicates; validate exits, access traces, faults, and throughput.
Run ConflictMask-32 differential cases with indexed stores, faulting predicates, and guard pages; record pre-exit accesses, conflicts, faults, and speedups.
ConflictMask-32 found 2/32 exit mismatches: offset indexed stores overlapped predicate loads by bytes but escaped start-address conflict masks.
Replace start-address masks with checked byte-interval overlap tests; scalarize overflow or unproven bounds, then rerun ConflictMask-32.
Implement checked byte-interval conflict masks, then rerun ConflictMask-32 against scalar exit lanes, store traces, first faults, and access bounds.
Checked byte-interval masks matched scalar exits, store traces, and first faults in 32/32 ConflictMask cases, with zero beyond-exit accesses.
Do checked byte-interval masks outperform 4-lane guarded prefixes on indexed-store kernels while keeping all three speedups above 1.3×?
Checked byte-interval masks will outperform 4-lane guarded prefixes on indexed-store kernels while maintaining ≥1.3× scalar throughput across all three.
Benchmark corrected byte-interval masks against 4-lane prefixes on three indexed-store kernels; verify scalar-equivalent traces and ≥1.3× speedups.
On the three indexed-store kernels, compare checked byte-interval masks with 4-lane prefixes; log scalar-relative throughput and exit/fault/store traces.
Byte-interval masks matched scalar traces and delivered 1.36×/1.37×/1.35× versus 4-lane prefixes’ 1.31×/1.34×/1.32×.
Choose checked byte-interval masks over start-address conflicts and 4-lane prefixes: correct indexed overlaps and 1.35–1.37× throughput.
Apply intra-iteration SLP to independent arithmetic and proven-nonfaulting loads, leaving exit checks, faulting accesses, and stores scalar-ordered.
Can intra-iteration SLP exceed 1.3× on all three kernels despite scalar exit checks and ordered stores?
Packing four independent arithmetic chains per iteration will achieve ≥1.3× on all three kernels without reordering exits, faults, or stores.
Prototype four-chain SLP after scalar predicate checks; compare scalar traces and optimized-scalar throughput on three exit-alias kernels.
Run SLP4 on three exit-alias kernels, comparing optimized-scalar cycles/iteration, exit lanes, store traces, first faults, and beyond-exit accesses.
SLP4 comparison report records cycles/iteration, exit lanes, store traces, first faults, and beyond-exit accesses for three kernels.
Audit the SLP4 report for trace equivalence and recompute scalar-relative speedups from cycles/iteration on all three kernels.
SLP4 matched scalar exits, stores, faults, and access bounds, but achieved only 1.12×/1.18×/1.09× versus optimized scalar.
Profile SLP4’s scalar predicate/store bottlenecks and test eight-chain packing plus software pipelining against the three 1.09–1.18× baselines.
Using SLP4’s report, profile predicate/store stalls and benchmark eight-chain SLP with software pipelining; verify scalar-equivalent fault and store traces.
Software-pipelined SLP4 matched scalar traces and reached 1.31×/1.33×/1.32×; SLP8 improved throughput by at most 0.02×.
Can software-pipelined SLP4 avoid beyond-exit preloads on guard-page loops while retaining ≥1.3× on all three kernels?
Predicate-gated software-pipelined SLP4, not packing alone, preserves zero beyond-exit loads on guard-page loops while retaining ≥1.3× on three kernels.
Gate SLP4 pipeline loads after scalar predicate checks; rerun guard-page ExitAlias-12 and three-kernel throughput benchmarks.
Use SLP4’s scalar baseline to test predicate-gated pipelining on guard-page ExitAlias-12 and three kernels; record access traces and speedups.
Gated SLP4 matched scalar exits, stores, and faults at 1.31×/1.33×/1.32×, but one ExitAlias-12 case read beyond exit.
Reject pipelined SLP4 despite ≥1.3× throughput: gated loads still access beyond exit; ordinary SLP4 misses the throughput target.
Certify exit-free chunks using register-only monotone bounds; vectorize proven-safe accesses and ordered stores, scalarizing uncertified chunks.
Which monotone exit predicates admit register-only chunk certification without overlooking intervening aliasing stores or earlier faulting accesses?
Final-lane bounds certify affine induction-variable exits when arithmetic cannot overflow, predicates are store-independent, and preceding accesses cannot fault.
Implement checked affine final-lane certificates; scalarize store-dependent predicates and unproven faults, then test exits, traces, and speedups.
Run MonotoneExit-20 with overflowing affine bounds, aliasing predicates, and guard pages; compare certificates, scalar traces, faults, and accesses.
MonotoneExit-20 found 2/20 exit mismatches: signed induction wrap passed the final-lane certificate despite a checked address offset.
Check induction endpoints in widened signed arithmetic before certification; reject wraparound chunks, then rerun MonotoneExit-20.
Add widened signed endpoint checks and rerun MonotoneExit-20, comparing scalar exit lanes, store traces, fault addresses, and beyond-exit accesses.
Widened endpoint checks matched scalar exits, stores, faults, and access bounds in 20/20 MonotoneExit cases; wraparound chunks scalarized.
Do widened affine certificates reach 1.3× on three exit-alias kernels after store-dependent predicates and fault-uncertain chunks scalarize?
Benchmark widened affine certificates on three exit-alias kernels; track certified-chunk share, scalar-equivalent traces, and optimized-scalar speedups.
Measure widened-certificate eligibility and speedup on three indexed-store exit kernels; audit scalar exits, store traces, faults, and accesses.
Widened certificates preserved scalar traces; 22%/31%/27% chunk eligibility yielded 1.08×/1.13×/1.10× speedups.
Defer affine certification as primary path: widened checks restore correctness, but 22–31% eligibility limits speedups to 1.08–1.13×.
